question.text: What will the IEA's November 2026 Oil Market Report give as Venezuela's crude oil supply for October 2026 (million barrels per day)?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number reported in the 'Venezuela' row of the 'OPEC+ crude oil production' table (values in million barrels per day) in the IEA's Oil Market Report – November 2026, scheduled for release at 10:00 Paris time on 13 November 2026 (release notice: https://www.iea.org/events/oil-market-report-november-2026). The relevant figure is the one in the column headed 'Oct 2026 Supply' — i.e. the column for the most recent month shown in that table, Venezuela's crude oil supply for October 2026; for the table's format and scale, the same table in the October 2026 edition (https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-october-2026) lists Venezuela at 1.16 mb/d for August 2026 and 1.16 mb/d for September 2026. Resolution uses the figure as first published in that 13 November 2026 edition, expressed in million barrels per day; if the table is not publicly displayed on iea.org, the figure quoted from that same edition by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: Revisions published later (for example in the December 2026 Oil Market Report or in IEA data files) are ignored. Only the Venezuela row of the 'OPEC+ crude oil production' table is used — not the 'Sustainable Capacity' column, not Venezuelan production figures cited elsewhere in the report's text, and not figures from other IEA publications. If the November 2026 edition does not report a Venezuela crude oil supply figure for October 2026 (row absent, or the October 2026 column blank), the question is annulled.

I could not independently check the brief's figures (Venezuela at 1.16 mb/d for Aug and for Sep 2026, sustainable capacity 1.12 mb/d), so they rest on the question text. [IEA Oct OMR](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-october-2026)
- The November OMR comes out on 2026-11-13 at 10:00 Paris time. The figure that counts is the "Oct 2026 Supply" column of the "OPEC+ crude oil production" table.
- An earlier sign the IEA is cautious on Venezuela: in July 2026 it cut its supply estimate, partly because Venezuelan output came in lower than forecast. [oilandgas360](https://www.oilandgas360.com/iea-cuts-oil-supply-estimate-on-lower-u-s-and-venezuelan-output/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No IEA, OPEC secondary-source or survey (Reuters, Bloomberg, Platts) estimate of Venezuela's October output has been published that I could find. A search for a Reuters October survey turned up nothing.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: NABEP restarted the Zuata 2 (Petrocedeño) furnace in the Orinoco Belt on Oct 31, after five years idle. This mainly affects November output onward. [wallstreet-online](https://www.wallstreet-online.de/nachricht/21626070-nabep-wichtigen-orinoco-bandofen-rahmen-fortgesetzten-produktionsoffensive-betrieb)
- 2026-11-01: NABEP said its rig count will rise to 41 in November, toward a goal of 60. Its output was 223,509 boe/d, a figure that includes gas and has not been audited. [discoveryalert](https://discoveryalert.com/analysis/venezuela-oil-production-rig-shortfall-november-2026/)
- 2026-11-02: Bloomberg reported that Venezuelan crude loadings fell 25% in October to about 809 kb/d, an eight-month low. It cited freight costs (Aframax rates to the US Gulf peaked at $13.85/bbl in early October, then fell to $9.41), autumn refinery maintenance, a 27% m-o-m drop in US demand, and PDVSA's refusal to cut prices. China has bought no Venezuelan crude for 10 straight months. The article says nothing about production, storage or output cuts. [TT/Bloomberg](https://www.ttnews.com/articles/freight-surge-venezuela-oil), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-02/freight-surge-pushes-venezuelan-oil-exports-to-eight-month-low)
  - This matters because a fall in exports this large could fill storage and limit output, or could lead the IEA to be cautious about any October increase. That is my inference, not something a source states.
- 2026-10-26: Oil Minister Obregón put national output at 1.252 mb/d. NABEP reported a record 115 kb/d in the west on Oct 23 and 223.5 kboe/d on Oct 19, about 20 kb/d more than in August. [Rigzone/Bloomberg](https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/pentagons_venezuelan_oil_partner_boosts_output-26-oct-2026-184932-article/)
- 2026-10-23: PDVSA reported 1.252 mb/d, its highest since 2019, with the western region at 382.5 kb/d. [teleSUR](https://www.telesurenglish.net/venezuela-oil-production/)
- 2026-10-17: Acting president Delcy Rodríguez said about $76bn of oil investment is expected over five years. [US News](https://www.usnews.com/news/top-news/articles/2026-10-17/venezuela-expects-nearly-76-billion-in-oil-investment-over-five-years-acting-president-says)
- 2026-10-13: OPEC data: Venezuela's government-reported figures were 1.201 mb/d for Aug and 1.206 mb/d for Sep. OPEC's secondary-source estimates were about 1.13 mb/d for Aug and 1.15 mb/d for Sep, so the official figure was about 56 kb/d higher in September. The government's Q3 average was 1.202 mb/d. [Rio Times](https://www.riotimesonline.com/venezuela-oil-output-opec-september-2026/)
- 2026-10-02: Reuters put September exports at about 1.08 mb/d, down from about 1.19 mb/d in August. [Curaçao Chronicle](https://www.curacaochronicle.com/post/unknown/venezuelas-oil-exports-fall-9-as-rising-shipping-costs-hit-pdvsa-sales)
- 2026-07-27: Columbia's Center on Global Energy Policy said the June 24 earthquakes could slow the oil recovery. It put output at about 1.2 mb/d in June, in what looks like official terms. [CGEP](https://www.energypolicy.columbia.edu/new-venezuelan-oil-regulations-offer-promise-but-politics-and-quake-recovery-threaten-investment/)

- How the IEA's numbers have behaved:
  - Month to month, first-print changes have been 0 to +0.04 mb/d.
  - Since August the IEA figure has sat about 0.04 to 0.05 mb/d below the official one.
  - The IEA kept its earlier months unchanged when it published the next report (July stayed 1.12, August stayed 1.16).
- If October's official average were about 1.23 to 1.25 mb/d and the gap stayed the same, the IEA figure would be roughly 1.18 to 1.21. This is arithmetic, not a forecast. The lower exports and the IEA's habit of holding the newest month flat point the other way, toward about 1.16.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 10 days. The IEA November OMR is released on 13 November 2026 at 10:00 Paris time.

(b) **Latest known value:** the October 2026 OMR (14 October 2026) gave Venezuela 1.16 mb/d for September 2026, the same as August.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 1.16 mb/d. The IEA has held its newest month flat before.

(d) **If the trend continued:** two cases.
- If the June to August pace of +0.04 mb/d per month resumed, the figure would be about 1.20 mb/d.
- If the IEA keeps its usual gap of about 0.04 to 0.05 mb/d below an official October average of about 1.23 to 1.25, the figure would be about 1.18 to 1.21 mb/d.

(e) **Historical variation:** first-print changes from month to month have been 0 to +0.04 mb/d. Larger moves of ±0.05 or more are uncommon outside shocks.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- There is no direct market or analyst forecast of the IEA figure.
- PDVSA's spot reading of 1.252 mb/d on 23 October points upward.
- October loadings fell 25% to about 809 kb/d, an eight-month low. This could make the IEA cautious or point to storage limits on output, so it argues for a flat or lower figure.
- The early-November Reuters, Bloomberg and Platts surveys and OPEC's 11 November secondary-source figures are not yet out.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** the IEA reads the export collapse as forced shut-ins due to full storage, or as power outages, and cuts October to 1.10-1.13.
- **High:** the IEA accepts much of PDVSA's gain and the Nabep and Zulia ramp-up, showing 1.22-1.25 mb/d.

My most likely single value is 1.16, the flat figure. I put the median slightly above it because the evidence on production leans upward, while the weak exports widen the downside tail.
